title: The hospital accordion player who has been busking for 35 years

evidence_packet.title: The hospital accordion player who has been busking for 35 years
evidence_packet.lead: Volunteer John Jones, 84, has been entertaining patients and visitors with his musical talents
evidence_packet.summary: Volunteer John Jones, 84, has been entertaining patients and visitors with his musical talents
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The hospital accordion player who has been busking for 35 years - BBC News Image source, East Cheshire NHS Trust Image caption, John Jones taught himself to play the accordion after his father passed away By Mairead Smyth , North West and Lauren Hirst , North West Published 1 hour ago For 35 years, volunteer John Jones has been entertaining patients and visitors at Macclesfield District General Hospital by playing the accordion. The 84-year-old retired engineer discovered his love of the accordion as a child, watching his father play the instrument. "My dad played the accordion all the time and I could play the piano a little bit," he said. "When he died, I started messing around with his accordion. "One half is like a piano, but the other half is completely different with buttons. "I had to teach myself, but I really enjoyed it." He has since been using his musical talents to raise money for East Cheshire NHS Charity. John's volunteering began after visiting the hospital with his mother-in-law in 1991 where he saw an appeal for a CT scanner. He has since raised hundreds of thousands of pounds for the charity. "One of the nicest moments was about five years after helping to raise the money for the scanner, I had to have a CT scan myself," said John who has an MBE for services to charity. "The nurse said, 'That's ironic, you're using the scanner you helped pay for.' That really stayed with me." 'It's a privilege' The money has been used to fund a family room at the hospital intensive care unit, where his wife June died from sepsis in 2020. "She'd been in intensive care five years earlier with sepsis as well, but she managed to survive that one," said John, who also performs in care homes. title: Hunt for Tameside millionaire as £1m lottery jackpot unclaimed

evidence_packet.title: Hunt for Tameside millionaire as £1m lottery jackpot unclaimed
evidence_packet.lead: The missing millionaire has two months left to claim their winnings after entering a July draw
evidence_packet.summary: The missing millionaire has two months left to claim their winnings after entering a July draw
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The hunt is on to find Tameside's next millionaire The owner of a lottery ticket bought in the Greater Manchester borough this summer now only has two months left to claim their £1m prize Under National Lottery rules, winners must submit their claim within six months. In this case they must do so before 00:00 GMT on 28 December "The winning ticket could be tucked away somewhere completely ordinary while its owner has absolutely no idea they are a millionaire," said Andy Carter from National Lottery operator Allwyn "We'd love to find the person we've been looking for and turn this search into a celebration," Carter added "So, if you bought a ticket in the area, dig it out, check those numbers and help us find Tameside's missing millionaire

Officers from Greater Manchester Police (GMP) were called to Market Street at 19:00 GMT on Tuesday. A GMP spokesperson said a 13-year-old boy was found and taken to hospital with potentially life-changing injuries, while two boys, aged 14 and 16, were arrested on suspicion of affray. A 14-year-old boy was stabbed at Manchester's Arndale shopping centre on Saturday, 17 October, and was taken to hospital with injuries consistent with a stab wound, while two other 14-year-old boys were arrested. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Council says e-scooter trial could begin in 2027 - BBC News Image source, LDRS Image caption, Manchester City Council said the scheme could be up and running next summer By Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 28 October 2026 People in Manchester could be travelling around on a fleet of electric scooters next year after plans for a new trial were announced. Manchester City Council is putting together proposals for the scheme and said in a report that it could begin in summer 2027, although the authority added it had not yet considered an operator for the e-scooters. The plans come off the back of the Lime scooter scheme in Salford which Salford Council said had been a major success. A council spokesperson stressed that a decision on whether to proceed with an e-scooter trial had not yet been made, and was conditional on backing from Greater Manchester Police and other groups. Image source, LDRS Image caption, E-scooters were launched in Salford in September 2020 They said provisional approval had been received from the Department for Transport (DfT) for the council to develop a proposal, and "officers are currently undertaking work to assess future benefits, risks and how an e-scooter scheme could work in practice in Manchester". Summer 2027 was the latest a trial could start in line with DfT requirements for new trials, they added. The council's report on e-scooters said they could offer Manchester residents and visitors a "popular zero-emission transport mode" to get around the city. An e-scooter trial was launched in Salford in 2020 and the city has continued to renew the scheme every two years since then, the Local Democracy Reporting Service said. The money will be invested in the Bury Market project as part of the government's Growth Mission Fund. More than £33m has so far been invested in the Greater Manchester town's market area, including a £20m grant from the Conservative government in 2024 . "Securing this funding has taken sustained work by the council - with the support of MP James Frith's campaigning in parliament," said Bury councillor Charlotte Morris. "It's a fantastic result for Bury - Bury Market is the jewel in our town centre's crown." Image caption, Bury's Indoor Market Hall closed in October 2023 Bury Council said the latest funding announcement would build on the town's long-term regeneration plans and address the former Indoor Market Hall's condition and enable its future use. The Indoor Market Hall closed in October 2023 following the discovery of reinforced autoclaved aerated concrete (RAAC). Since then, new outdoor market canopies have been erected and a new food, drink and events venue is due to open in November. title: Children at council-run home illegally tattooed each other

evidence_packet.title: Children at council-run home illegally tattooed each other
evidence_packet.lead: The children had tattooed themselves and others using illegally bought kit, Ofsted found
evidence_packet.summary: The children had tattooed themselves and others using illegally bought kit, Ofsted found
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Children at council-run home illegally tattooed each other - BBC News Image source, PA Media Image caption, Inspectors found staff at the home in Salford had "failed to act" when a child repeatedly tattooed themselves, other children in the home, and "reportedly peers in the community" By Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 28 October 2026 Young people at a council-owned children's home were found to have tattooed themselves and others with illegally bought kit, a government watchdog found. An Ofsted inspector discovered staff at the home in Salford had "failed to act" when a child repeatedly tattooed themselves, other children in the home, and "reportedly peers in the community". The home was rated 'inadequate' by Ofsted and handed three compliance notices to improve children's safety and welfare. A Salford City Council spokesperson said: "We accepted the findings of the inspection in full and have already taken swift action to address the issues raised, resulting in recent positive feedback from Ofsted." "Children now have multiple permanent tattoos which may impact their future choices and opportunities," the inspector wrote in their report. "And children did not receive appropriate medical support and remained exposed to potential health risks." The report also found that staff applied consequences "punitively", with children's bus fares regularly withheld, including for travel to family contact. Inspectors described the practice as "excessive and unreasonable" and noted the type of punishment "does not promote children's welfare or relationships with their families". evidence_packet.evidence_text: This year marks 100 years since Wythenshawe Hall was donated to Manchester Corporation At the time, the city was in urgent need of more housing In 1920 an urban planner called Patrick Abercrombie identified Wythenshawe as the only undeveloped land suitable for building a housing estate close to Manchester To turn his proposal into a reality, Ernest and Shena Simon bought Wythenshawe Hall from Robert Henry Grenville Tatton in 1926, which they donated to the city's corporation (now known as the council) The idea was that people could be rehoused away from industrial Manchester into what became known as the "Garden City" To celebrate 100 years, BBC North West Tonight has spoken to 100 people from the area about what Wythenshawe means to them

The uniformed cops are part of the brand-new Transport Police and Crime Command team, also known as TPACC The unit has been created to provide coverage of the roads, Metrolink and bus services across Greater Manchester. For two travellers, the misery is compounded as they are carted away in handcuffs by police officers who were diligently patrolling the Metrolink These officers and perhaps arrests will soon be a familiar site for voyaging Mancunians. The uniformed cops are part of the brand-new Transport Police and Crime Command team, also known as TPACC The unit has been created to provide coverage of the roads, Metrolink and bus services across Greater Manchester. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Tributes pour in for Stockport mum-of-five who helped thousands of animals with RSPCA Sonia Hulme was 'deeply determined to make a difference' Add to preferred sources Comments News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 18:34, 28 Oct 2026 View 3 I Tributes have been paid to a much-loved mum-of-five who saved thousands of animals in a career spanning more than 20 years at the RSPCA . Sonia Hulme, from Stockport , tragically died aged 50 following a short illness relating to cancer she had three years ago She had worked as a frontline animal rescue officer for the RSPCA across the North West, and will be laid to rest in the uniform she proudly wore. RSPCA Chief Inspector Nina Small, who is in charge of the Greater Manchester inspectorate group, said: “Sonia's dedication and compas "She was tenacious and deeply determined to make a difference to animals, supporting her colleagues with her wealth of knowledge and advice. Regardless of whether it was convenient, Sonia always made time to help an animal in need "Quick-witted and brave, she was not afraid to speak up when she felt it mattered. She was such a unique individual and will be missed by so many." Sonia began her RSPCA career working to rehabilitate rescued animals at the charity's Stockport branch, before moving into frontline work. She spent 12 years working with officers in Cheshire and Merseyside, before eight years as an RSPCA officer in Greater Manchester

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Manchester Airport passengers miss Ryanair flights in ‘horrendous’ security queues One passenger described the situation as a 'shambles' and claimed they waited two hours to pass through security Add to preferred sources Comments Ne A Manchester Airport passenger has spoken about ‘shocking’ queues at Terminal 3 Security on Tuesday (October 27) evening which resulted in them and others missing their flights. Tony Cooke and his wife Keeley claim that they were stuck in security for around two hours which meant The couple, who are from Manchester but live in Alicante, had arrived at security at 6.50pm, ahead of their 9pm flight to Spain. Despite arriving in plenty of time, they found themselves caught up in lengthy queues at Terminal 3 Security “The queue at security was just horrendous. We were held back at the barriers where you have your ticket scanned, and then once we were through it was just nose to tail,” Mr Cooke said “There seemed to be only one out of the six security lanes working, it looked like a rostering issue to me. We were told that staff had also been sent to Terminal 2 due to an ‘incident’.” View 3 Images Terminal 3 Manchester Airport (Image: Manchester Airport)

evidence_packet.lead: Old Trafford ‘No indication’ of who carried out cyber attack impacting thousands of Greater Manchester residents Data from around 12,000 people was accessed 'without authorisation' in last month's hack Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Ric Investigations into a cyber

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Old Trafford ‘No indication’ of who carried out cyber attack impacting thousands of Greater Manchester residents Data from around 12,000 people was accessed 'without authorisation' in last month's hack Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Ric Investigations into a cyber attack that has impacted thousands of Greater Manchester residents are no closer to finding the culprit L&Q Housing, which has offices in Old Trafford , saw its systems breached by hackers at the end of September . Emails and webforms sent by around 12,000 residents were accessed ‘without authorisation’, prompting the company to launch a ‘comprehensive’ investigation into how this But an update emailed to residents on Tuesday, October 27, and seen by the Local Democracy Reporting Service reveals that those investigations have not ‘yet provided any indication of who might have been responsible’ L&Q also said it has had ‘no reports of anyone attempting to use the information accessed maliciously’, adding it has ‘seen no further unauthorised attempts to access [its] systems’ The firm previously stated it believed the incident to be limited to online contacts from residents, with systems containing residents’ personal details, financial information, data about homes and tenancies, and information relating to suppliers and partners remaining ‘secure’

Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 16:13, 28 Oct 2026 View Image Baron Bryan Davies of Oldham h Former MP for Oldham, Lord Bryan Davies, has died at the age of 86 The late British Labour politician first entered the Houses of Parliament as the Member of Parliament (MP) for Enfield North in London which he held for five years between 1974 and 1979 before losing to the Conservatives . He was then elected 13 years later in 1992 as the MP for However in 1997, that constituency was abolished due to boundary changes and Baron Davies was beaten in the Labour selection process for the new constituency of Oldham West and Royton by Michael Meacher. Later that year, he was given a life peerage in the House of Lords and subse He held this position until July 9 2024 where he was removed as a member because of non-attendance. The Association of Former Members of Parliament said he died in October 2026 Baron Davies served as Government Deputy Chief Whip in the House of Lords from 2003 to 2010, and as usual for a holder of that position, also held the position of Captain of the Yeomen of the Guard

Earlier today, Chancellor John Healey set out the 2026 Budget , the first under Andy Burnham's leadership He has promised to use his autumn statement to give households and businesses “breathing space today” from everyday costs. Speaking in the House of Commons, the Chancellor promised “a Budget for the working people of Britain” His announcements included a cut to VAT on electricity being extended to July, taking £50 off the annual price cap, alongside a £100 household energy payment to people in council tax bands A to D to help them deal with soaring bills “through to the spring” He also told MPs he will raise the threshold for small business rate relief for retail hospitality and leisure businesses to £18,000, and freeze rates for all other firms in these sectors in real terms. The national minimum wage and national living wage will also increase by 3.9% The chancellor also confirmed new rates for the state pension and other benefits from April next year, as well as new tax rules that will prevent low income state pensioners paying income tax when the full state pension amount exceeds the personal allowance. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bee Network Greater Manchester has a brand-new police force as first arrests made at Piccadilly People were pictured arrested at Manchester Piccadilly by the brand-new police team Add to preferred sources Comments News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 06 The rain lashes the platform of the Piccadilly tram stop as commuters brave a miserable Monday morning. For two travellers, the misery is compounded as they are carted away in handcuffs by police officers who were diligently patrolling the Metrolink These officers and perhaps arrests will soon be a familiar site for voyaging Mancunians. The uniformed cops are part of the brand-new Transport Police and Crime Command team, also known as TPACC The unit has been created to provide coverage of the roads, Metrolink and bus services across Greater Manchester. It officially launches on Thursday (October 29), but officers from the group were already in operation on Monday (October 26) The team was originally signed off by Andy Burnham during his stint as a mayor. The project has been previously referred to as the GMP’s ‘11th district’, but the unit has had to wait for the greenlight due to a series of elections View 4 Images Officers will tackle crime and anti-social behaviour on the transport network (Image: Kenny Brown | Manchester Evening News)

evidence_packet.summary: Crime Inside Manchester's early prison release scheme As prisons across release inmates early after serving just one-third of their sentences, victim advocates and probation unions warn the government's £100m Sentencing Act reforms risk putting domest Add to preferred sources Com
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Crime Inside Manchester's early prison release scheme As prisons across release inmates early after serving just one-third of their sentences, victim advocates and probation unions warn the government's £100m Sentencing Act reforms risk putting domest Add to preferred sources Comments News Annie Gouk and Stephen Topping Senior reporter 05:57, 29 Oct 2026 Thousands of offenders will be released early from prison by next summer. It's a significant step in the government's attempts to grapple with a prison capacity crisis - but i The contentious scheme affects prisons in England and Wales - including Strangeways, Forest Bank, Hindley, Buckley Hall and Styal. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Trouble in a corner of Greater Manchester's 'toughest place to be a child' It started with persistent games of knock and run and led to fireworks 'hurled towards a double pram'. But the city is also at the sharp end of a 'national emergency'. Add to preferred sources Comments News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 05:56, 29 Oct 2026 By the time police issued three Facebook posts about it in six days, events had reached a tipping point. Officers slapped a 48-hour dispersal order on Ordsall , in Salford , after a 'large g Days later police were back in the neighbourhood, investigating 'the misuse of fireworks, criminal damage and bin fires' in Ordsall Park. Two arrests were made, other youths were identified and neighbours were urged to come forward with any concerns they had For residents living on the edge of Ordsall Park, those incidents in early October were just the tip of the iceberg. A campaign of 'harassment' and nuisance has been targeted at locals for more than a year, the Manchester Evening News has been told Multiple residents told the M.E.N. they were considering leaving their homes and moving elsewhere as a result. And with Bonfire Night on the horizon, memories of last November 5 - when fireworks were hurled down the street near Ordsall Park, narrowly missing homes and cars - are "We've been getting harassed on this street for most of this year," one Hulton Street resident told the M.E.N. "Kids playing knock and run, but every day. That's why we've all got [CCTV] cameras."

Sonia Hulme, from Stockport , tragically died aged 50 following a short illness relating to cancer she had three years ago She had worked as a frontline animal rescue officer for the RSPCA across the North West, and will be laid to rest in the uniform she proudly wore. RSPCA Chief Inspector Nina Small, who is in charge of the Greater Manchester inspectorate group, said: “Sonia's dedication and compas "She was tenacious and deeply determined to make a difference to animals, supporting her colleagues with her wealth of knowledge and advice. Regardless of whether it was convenient, Sonia always made time to help an animal in need "Quick-witted and brave, she was not afraid to speak up when she felt it mattered. She was such a unique individual and will be missed by so many." Sonia began her RSPCA career working to rehabilitate rescued animals at the charity's Stockport branch, before moving into frontline work. She spent 12 years working with officers in Cheshire and Merseyside, before eight years as an RSPCA officer in Greater Manchester

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Manchester Airport passengers miss Ryanair flights in ‘horrendous’ security queues One passenger described the situation as a 'shambles' and claimed they waited two hours to pass through security Add to preferred sources Comments Ne A Manchester Airport passenger has spoken about ‘shocking’ queues at Terminal 3 Security on Tuesday (October 27) evening which resulted in them and others missing their flights. Tony Cooke and his wife Keeley claim that they were stuck in security for around two hours which meant The couple, who are from Manchester but live in Alicante, had arrived at security at 6.50pm, ahead of their 9pm flight to Spain. Despite arriving in plenty of time, they found themselves caught up in lengthy queues at Terminal 3 Security “The queue at security was just horrendous. We were held back at the barriers where you have your ticket scanned, and then once we were through it was just nose to tail,” Mr Cooke said “There seemed to be only one out of the six security lanes working, it looked like a rostering issue to me. We were told that staff had also been sent to Terminal 2 due to an ‘incident’.” View 3 Images Terminal 3 Manchester Airport (Image: Manchester Airport)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Old Trafford ‘No indication’ of who carried out cyber attack impacting thousands of Greater Manchester residents Data from around 12,000 people was accessed 'without authorisation' in last month's hack Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Ric Investigations into a cyber attack that has impacted thousands of Greater Manchester residents are no closer to finding the culprit L&Q Housing, which has offices in Old Trafford , saw its systems breached by hackers at the end of September . Emails and webforms sent by around 12,000 residents were accessed ‘without authorisation’, prompting the company to launch a ‘comprehensive’ investigation into how this But an update emailed to residents on Tuesday, October 27, and seen by the Local Democracy Reporting Service reveals that those investigations have not ‘yet provided any indication of who might have been responsible’ L&Q also said it has had ‘no reports of anyone attempting to use the information accessed maliciously’, adding it has ‘seen no further unauthorised attempts to access [its] systems’ The firm previously stated it believed the incident to be limited to online contacts from residents, with systems containing residents’ personal details, financial information, data about homes and tenancies, and information relating to suppliers and partners remaining ‘secure’

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre Four teens arrested after boy, 13, stabbed in Manchester city centre A teenage boy remains in a stable condition in hospital Add to preferred sources News Amy Walker Court reporter 16:36, 28 Oct 2026 View 3 Images Police outside Four teenage boys have been arrested after a 13-year-old boy was stabbed in Manchester city centre. Officers swarmed the Arndale shopping centre on Tuesday evening (October 27) following reports of a stabbing Police taped off a lift in the shopping centre near the Roller's café while multiple police vehicles were seen on High Street and Withy Grove, including a forensics van. Greater Manchester Police previously said it was called out to reports of a stabbing on Market Street , outsid In an update, the force said that a boy, 13, was found with injuries consistent with knife wounds. He was taken to hospital where he remains in a stable condition Three boys - aged 14, 15 and 16 - have been arrested on suspicion of affray and remain in custody for questioning. Another boy, aged 13, was arrested on suspicion of possession of a bladed article Enquiries are ongoing to establish the full circumstances. There will be an increased police presence in the area as the investigation continues, the force said

Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 16:13, 28 Oct 2026 View Image Baron Bryan Davies of Oldham h Former MP for Oldham, Lord Bryan Davies, has died at the age of 86 The late British Labour politician first entered the Houses of Parliament as the Member of Parliament (MP) for Enfield North in London which he held for five years between 1974 and 1979 before losing to the Conservatives . He was then elected 13 years later in 1992 as the MP for However in 1997, that constituency was abolished due to boundary changes and Baron Davies was beaten in the Labour selection process for the new constituency of Oldham West and Royton by Michael Meacher. Later that year, he was given a life peerage in the House of Lords and subse He held this position until July 9 2024 where he was removed as a member because of non-attendance. evidence_packet.evidence_text: How a sweatshop empire is Manchester-washing its reputation “I can’t always be in LA,” reads one TikTok caption, “someone has to hold it down in Rochdale.” It’s written over a model strutting through a leatherwear shoot. She’s wearing Musera, which looks to be Manchester’s friendliest, chicest new clothing label — launched in 2024 from an From this Newton Street office, a band of young designers turn out a stream of trend pieces: low-rise trousers and asymmetric tops, distressed knitwear and leopard-print flares, western fringed jumpers and A-level prom gowns. Their Instagram bio lauds the brand as “Est. MCR.” Over a million people watched the staff dancing around their Northern Quarter office to Whigfield’s Saturday Night on TikTok. More still tuned in to a video showing them kitted out in Musera for Drake’s performance at Co-op Live last year. And who knows how many have sidestepped “Be a muse in your own era,” goes their slogan; presumably also the source of their similarly recondite name. Their Instagram captions are a list of internet cliches verging on parody. “My blood type is iced latte,” reads one post Looking at this well-curated online presence, you might well be convinced that Musera is, as they suggest, Manchester through and through

evidence_packet.lead: The incident saw a large part of the town centre cordoned off for a day
evidence_packet.summary: The incident saw a large part of the town centre cordoned off for a day
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The incident saw a large part of the town centre cordoned off for a day Share on WhatsApp Share via Email A man has been found guilty of trying to murder a stranger during a series of random attacks in Altrincham town centre last year Nathan Peters, 23, of Lock Lane, Partington, was convicted by a jury of the attempted murder of Max Morrison, who was stabbed four times in the early hours of Sunday 30 November 2025 Mr Morrison collapsed nearby and went into cardiac arrest, Manchester Crown Court heard Peters had admitted wounding with intent in relation to Mr Morrison but denied attempted murder. The jury was asked to decide whether he intended to kill him He had already pleaded guilty to wounding with intent after slashing the face of Mr Morrison's friend, Harrison Brannan, who had stepped in to try to stop the stabbing

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The proposals prompted a lengthy debate at Trafford Council's Executive meeting Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Thorley Lane car park in Timperley Plans to introduce parking charges at Thorley Lane car park in Timperley have come under fierce criticism from local councillors, who warn they could damage independent businesses and drive shoppers away from th The proposals prompted a lengthy debate at Trafford Council's Executive meeting on Monday night, with councillors questioning whether the authority would listen to widespread opposition from residents, traders and community organisations The introduction of charges at the currently free car park forms part of the council's draft budget for 2027/28 , which includes plans to generate an additional £250,000 a year from parking charges across Trafford Councillor Newgrosh said there was near-unanimous opposition to the plans among local organisations "Every local organisation, whether it's civic society, local traders, the volunteers that run the community centre, all residents are pretty much united in our position against this," he told the meeting

title: Altrincham Grammar School for Girls proposes admissions shake-up that could disadvantage local pupils

evidence_packet.title: Altrincham Grammar School for Girls proposes admissions shake-up that could disadvantage local pupils
evidence_packet.lead: A public consultation has opened on changes that could affect who secures one of the sought-after grammar school's 204 Year 7 places
evidence_packet.summary: A public consultation has opened on changes that could affect who secures one of the sought-after grammar school's 204 Year 7 places
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A public consultation has opened on changes that could affect who secures one of the sought-after grammar school's 204 Year 7 places Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Girls living close to Altrincham Grammar School for Girls could lose priority for places to children attending four designated primary schools under proposed changes to its admissions policy A public consultation has opened on plans to give pupils from four primary schools belonging to the same academy trust as AGGS priority over other applicants who have passed the entrance examination – even if they live closer to the school The proposals, which would take effect from September 2028, could have significant implications for Altrincham families whose daughters attend local primary schools outside Bright Futures Educational Trust Under the existing admissions system, girls who pass the entrance examination and live within the school's eight-mile catchment area are generally prioritised according to how close they live to AGGS, after higher-priority categories have been considered But the proposed arrangements would introduce a new category giving preference to qualifying pupils attending four primary schools within Bright Futures Educational Trust

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The new Transport Policing and Crime Command has been created to tackle crime and antisocial behaviour on the Bee Network The new squad will deliver a "significant increase" in visible policing and enforcement across the transport network, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said The dedicated unit, which will also cover the city's active travel routes and roads, has been formed with funding from the Mayor of Greater Manchester's budget It will be supported by control centre staff at GMP and Transport for Greater Manchester, which has access to CCTV cameras across bus stations, interchanges, tram stops and train stations Chief Constable Sir Stephen Watson said the aim was to "make the roads and public transport among the safest in the UK" Bev Craig, Mayor of Greater Manchester said the move would "bring together up to 300 police and safety officers, with high-profile patrols across our roads and the Bee Network"

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Lawrence Johnson, 26, of Dorking Avenue, was held on remand at HMP Liverpool after being charged with the murder of Alisha Samuels, who was found dead in Newton Heath on 15 October Footage seen by the BBC, thought to have been filmed from within the prison at the weekend, shows Johnson being attacked in a cell. In the video, inmates can be heard saying: "Bro, you're getting chopped up. Sit down, bro. Smash him up." A Prison Service spokesperson said the social media post was being investigated, adding "violence will not be tolerated in the prison estate" "Having a phone behind bars is unacceptable and we have ordered the immediate removal of these posts while investigating how this was able to happen," they said Johnson has also been charged with the attempted murder of a man A further three men have also been charged on suspicion of Samuels' murder, Greater Manchester Police earlier confirmed

title: Simon Richardson 'selfish' for crash but not murderer, jury told

evidence_packet.title: Simon Richardson 'selfish' for crash but not murderer, jury told
evidence_packet.lead: A motorist who dragged a cyclist trapped under his car for more than a mile was responsible for his death, but that did not make him a murderer, a court has heard Simon Richardson, 35, is on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court accused of the murder of head teacher Mic
evidence_packet.summary: A motorist who dragged a cyclist trapped under his car for more than a mile was responsible for his death, but that did not make him a murderer, a court has heard Simon Richardson, 35, is on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court accused of the murder of head teacher Mic
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A motorist who dragged a cyclist trapped under his car for more than a mile was responsible for his death, but that did not make him a murderer, a court has heard Simon Richardson, 35, is on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court accused of the murder of head teacher Michael Mullins, 56, who was knocked off his bike as he travelled home from Stretford Grammar School in Manchester Prosecutors say Richardson knew Mullins was underneath his car shortly after the collision but drove on anyway, which he denies Mullins became entangled in the suspension of Richardson's Volvo XC90 and was dragged for 2.2km (1.4 miles) after the collision in Warburton, near Altrincham, on 20 April The court heard Richardson drove through Give Way markings at a junction in Warburton and collided with Mullins, who went under his vehicle A motorcyclist followed a trail of blood and discovered Mullins alone and barely breathing as he lay on a grass verge in a secluded country lane in Lymm, Cheshire

title: Bolton Council to consider national changes to planning system - Bolton Council

evidence_packet.title: Bolton Council to consider national changes to planning system - Bolton Council
evidence_packet.lead: Bolton Council will hold a meeting on November 10 to consider national changes to the planning system
evidence_packet.summary: Bolton Council will hold a meeting on November 10 to consider national changes to the planning system
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Council to consider national changes to planning system – Bolton Council Published: Wednesday, 28th Oct 2026 Bolton Council will hold a meeting on November 10 to consider national changes to the planning system. What are the changes? Last year, the government updated the National Scheme of Delegation for planning applications. Under the changes, which come into effect on October 31, more applications would be decided by planning officers rather than by a committee of elected members. The government has said this would make planning applications quicker, more efficient and reduce the number of decisions overturned on appeal. Larger and more contentious applications would still need approval from planning committees. What happens next? For these changes to be implemented in Bolton, there must first be an amendment to the council constitution agreed by a vote at Full Council. At a meeting on October 7, Full Council voted against amending the constitution to incorporate the new National Scheme of Delegation. The matter will next be considered by Full Council on November 10. How will this impact my planning application? Nationally the new rules will apply from October 31. This means Bolton Council will not legally be allowed to hold Planning Committee Meetings or determine any planning applications, after this date unless and until the constitution is amended. The council will continue to receive and assess new and existing applications during this period. Unfortunately disruption to the planning system locally and delays to decisions are inevitable. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. evidence_packet.summary: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live […] The post Beat the Jams Autumn season announced appeared first on Band on the Wall
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Joshua Reed-Cooper and Mike Thomas will bring regional French cooking and an extensive wine list to the former TNQ site this winter Go to Manchester's Finest X profile The duo behind Stockport’s Michelin-recognised Cantaloupe are opening a new French restaurant in the Northern Quarter Joshua Reed-Cooper and Mike Thomas will open Rasade at 108 High Street – the former site of long-standing bistro TNQ – this winter, with a menu inspired by regional French cooking and built around seasonal produce The new restaurant is the latest project from the pair, who have worked in some of the city’s most notable kitchens Cooper’s CV includes Where The Light Gets In , Adam Reid at The French and mana , while he also ran Tine, a pop-up kitchen at Blossom Street Social. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. They are now, by his assessment, considerably less so. Downstairs has been redone, upstairs has new ones too, while a previously overlooked back room has been completely reworked

evidence_packet.lead: Posted by Manchester Digital Manchester Digital Festival 2027: Programme revealed as tickets go on sale
evidence_packet.summary: Five days. Five themes
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Five days. Five themes. One city shaping its digital future. The first Manchester Digital Festival takes place from 8–12 February 2027 with its biggest and boldest programme yet. Manchester Digital has unveiled the programme for Manchester Digital Festival 2027 (MDF27 ) , bringin Taking place from Monday 8 to Friday 12 February 2027 , the festival marks an exciting new chapter for Manchester Digital, building on the success of Digital Skills Festival and expanding its scope to celebrate the full breadth of Greater Manchester's digital and technology secto The launch also comes as Manchester Digital celebrates its 25th anniversary , providing an opportunity to reflect on the people, businesses and innovations that have shaped the region's tech ecosystem, while looking ahead to what comes next With 15 events already announced and more to come, the first wave of the MDF27 programme offers everything from industry conferences and leadership discussions to careers events, founder stories and opportunities to explore emerging technologies Tickets for most events are now available , with further announcements expected in the coming months Under the banner Building our digital tomorrow , MDF27 introduces a new five-day format, with each day dedicated to a different theme reflecting the opportunities and challenges facing Greater Manchester's digital and technology sector

title: Manchester Digital helps shape government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan | Manchester Digital

evidence_packet.title: Manchester Digital helps shape government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan | Manchester Digital
evidence_packet.lead: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities.
evidence_packet.summary: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Applications are now open for MentorHER Cohort 4 , Manchester Digital's mentoring programme connecting women at the beginning of their digital and technology careers with experienced professionals across the industry Launched to coincide with Ada Lovelace Day, the fourth cohort of MentorHER will run from January to July 2027, delivered through Manchester Digital's DigitalHER programme in partnership with Autotrader The six-month programme aims to help women build confidence, develop their professional skills and establish valuable connections as they navigate the early stages of their careers in digital and technology Applications are now open for both mentors and mentees, with a deadline of Sunday 8 November 2026 Building a successful career in technology is about more than technical skills. evidence_packet.summary: L-R: Simon Shaw, Anna Dick, Alastair Brown, Tripti Anil, Alan Jackson Simon Shaw, Delivery Director at Codurance, hosted the lunchtime session for tech leaders and introduced Codurance, which is a global software engineering consultancy that has run its Manchester office for 15 y
evidence_packet.evidence_text: L-R: Simon Shaw, Anna Dick, Alastair Brown, Tripti Anil, Alan Jackson Simon Shaw, Delivery Director at Codurance, hosted the lunchtime session for tech leaders and introduced Codurance, which is a global software engineering consultancy that has run its Manchester office for 15 years He was joined on the panel by Anna Dick, Chief Technology & Product Officer at Capsule; Alastair Brown, Group Director of AI and Technology at Peninsula; Tripti Anil, Senior Leader, Data & Analytics at Kellanova; and Alan Jackson, Director of Client Solutions at Codurance Talking about discovering how AI can be used in projects, Anna said that Capsule's initial three months of AI exploration across all its business teams built appetite for further experimentation, but it also got a little out of control. Some things needed revisiting and tidying u Alastair stressed product discipline in order to understand the business driver and the outcome you want. At Peninsula, one initiative focused on giving customers richer answers and delivered over £1m in revenue. He said success depends on strong sponsorship and expertise from wi Tripti described spending three years building data foundations at Kellanova, focusing on "the right things at the right time" and bringing business teams along on the journey. They started with UK field sales as a proof of concept initially

Since then, BGF has supported the group’s growth from a single branch of Rudy’s and Albert’s Schloss in Manchester to 44 sites across the UK. The exit has generated a return for BGF of 3.75x MM and Fynveur, an investment holding owned by Artal and advised by Invus, has acquired a majority stake in Mission Mars, to accelerate the further roll-out of both brands Mission Mars has delivered impressive growth through FY26, with five new openings all trading ahead of expectations. Several further openings are planned in the near term, including the first Rudy’s in Scotland – opening in Glasgow later this month. The group currently employs mo Roy Ellis, CEO of Mission Mars, said: “We’d like to thank BGF for their support over the past eight years. They backed us at the early stages of growth and have been a supportive partner as we’ve expanded across the UK “It has been clear from early conversations that there is a strong culture and ambition fit between Mission Mars, Artal and the Invus team. Our focus on a world-class product, guest experience, team engagement and sustainable long-term growth remains at the forefront of our plans

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A new exhibition at The Portico Library explores feminist themes of wellbeing, ageing and place in relation to magic and ritual healing Open now, Witches & Healers draws on Rosie Reed Hillman’s groundbreaking project Something That Was Ours , which explores what it means to be a witch today Hillman’s portraits of witches and healers are curated in dialogue with historic texts chosen by critical friends who identify with the practice of witchcraft and/or healing. The portraits, the books chosen, and their interpretation offer unique insights into the diverse lives an Using a mix of moving image and photography, the artwork builds a sensory and emotive portrait of women in midlife. Covering themes of menopause, mental health, climate change, and marital breakdown, this work explores the ways women have reclaimed the word witch and sought solac Speaking about the exhibition , Rosie Reed Hillman says: “I have worked to build rapport with contributors over the last four years and believe the intimate access conveyed in this project creates an exhibition that inspires empathy, curiosity and a greater understanding of issue “Women in midlife of all backgrounds are an overlooked demographic who want to see art and hear stories that reflect their experiences, and I hope this work speaks to them especially.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Little Wander in association with PBJ Management present Amy Matthews: Definitions of Toast Amy doesn't get angry and she's starting to feel left out, so she's on a quest to feel fury; from what she can discern from the world around her, it appears to be all the rage... literally Amy is navigating the joy of her first queer relationship whilst dusting herself off from a string of several alcoholic partners. You'd think she'd have plenty to be cross about, and yet, whilst everyone seems to be more furious than ever, she just can't seem to tap into her own This lack of wrath may also have something to do with a processing lag that is becoming increasingly disruptive - and comical - in her life. Her emotions seemed to be delivered by carrier pigeon, if they arrive at all This is a show about being Best Supporting Actor in one's own life, queer joy, and how a potion from 2002 cursed the world "Drily funny and giddily quirky." (The Scotsman)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. A hugely productive two-year loan at Old Trafford saw Tevez clinch consecutive Premier League titles, the Champions League , the Cara That was before he made the controversial decision to move to the Etihad in 2009 , where he eventually linked up with his Argentina team-mate. But despite the bond he shared with his countryman at City, he couldn't look beyond 'Wazza' while speaking to another former colleague, R "They are very different," said Tevez during an appearance on the Rio Ferdinand Presents channel when asked who was the better partner. "They are different but for me the best player...I don’t know how to say. Best partner. Yeah. The best partner." Tevez, who retired in 2022, spent an identical two-season spell playing alongside each player. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Carlos Tevez Carlos Tevez comes clean on real reason he left Man United for Man City Carlos Tevez has explained the reason for joining Manchester City after spending two years at Old Trafford Add to preferred sources Comments Sport Kieran Horn 22:30, 28 Oct 2026 Vi Carlos Tevez has admitted he joined Manchester City to get revenge on Sir Alex Ferguson for failing to keep Manchester United promises. The Argentine headed to Etihad Stadium in the summer of 2009 following a two-year loan spell at United from West Ham Despite a successful spell at Old Trafford , where he scored 34 goals in 99 appearances, the two parties failed to agree on a permanent deal. Real Madrid reportedly came in for Tevez but it was City that signed him for a British-record £47million in 2009 He spent four years at United's rivals and managed 73 goals in 148 games. And now Tevez, who was appearing on the Rio Ferdinand Presents channel , has revealed exactly why he made the move across Manchester The 42-year-old said: "Look, I feel like I left a lot, uh, at both teams. But if you make me choose, let's say, uh, I had a great time at United. The other team, uh, City, for me, was like a revenge for for, how can I put it, uh, I didn't get back what I gave." A two-year loan is not that common in football and was actually banned by FIFA in 2022 but Tevez was one of few to complete such a move

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Combined Authority ‘People want transparency’ - Greater Manchester’s housing loans over more than a decade to be scrutinised It comes after intense coverage of the city's relatioship with Abu Dhabi.
